transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping have concluded their third bilateral meeting
this year.
This one took place in Shenzhen on the sidelines of an economic summit.
Xi is hosting NPR's Deepa Shivarom reports.
Trump called his relationship with Xi "outstanding" and said their friendship has served the people
of the U.S. and China.
He said the U.S. and China have made improvements in their economic ties.
The two nations just a year ago were battling escalating tensions over tariffs.
Now, Trump says, "We've made it a fair relationship, and that's all we want, that's all we ask."
Trump says the U.S. and China share interests in ending the war between Russia and Ukraine.
Deepa Shivarom, NPR News, Shenzhen.
The meeting between Trump and Xi lasted roughly an hour.
The two broke for launch.
And now, Russian leader Vladimir Putin has joined them for their trilateral meeting.
It got underway a short time ago.
It's the first ever between the leaders of the three countries.
Along with Ukraine, the war in Iran, nuclear proliferation, trade tensions, and artificial
intelligence are believed to be on the agenda.
The highest-ranking Democrat on the House Oversight Committee is telling President Trump's aides
and family members to preserve documents and records ahead of expected investigations.
President Piers Franco Ordonez reports the White House is accusing Democrats of working
against the American people.
The Democratic Congressman Robert Garcia is poised to become the next chair of the committee
that is expected to lead many of these investigations.
Garcia sent out letters to over a dozen of President Trump's aides and allies, including
Chief of Staff Stephen Miller and family like Donald Trump Jr.
The White House criticized the effort, saying that the president is willing to work with
anyone on behalf of hardworking Americans, but that Democrats are pursuing "cham investigations"
and "radical left policies."
Garcia said his focuses on four main areas, including allegations of family corruption,
corporate corruption, DHS misconduct, and the White House Epstein cover-up.
Franco Ordonez, NPR News.
Reports of emergency are in effect in multiple Florida cities where heavy rain sparked flooding
Wednesday.
Dean Trantralis is the mayor of Fort Lauderdale.
"I have declared a state of emergency for the city of Fort Lauderdale.
Broward County has already done the same.
Our community receives significant rainfall overnight, and several of our neighborhoods
are experiencing significant flooding."
And officials are warning of more flooding, forecasters say a slow-moving storm that has
flooded portions of South Florida is expected to hang around through Friday.
Preliminary figures show a foot of rain fell in portions of Broward County, the roof of
a synagogue collapsed from heavy rain, and authorities closed portions of the Florida
Turnpike and Interstate 95 because of high-water installed vehicles.
This is NPR.
In Gaza, there's only one crossing open where aid and commercial goods can enter.
And Pearson-Asbaba reports that it's controlled by Israel, which is facing growing international
pressure to allow winter essentials into the region.
Under the terms of the ceasefire, for the past 13 months, Israel was supposed to allow
600 trucks of supplies into Gaza every day.
But for about a year, the daily average has been closer to 200 trucks.
Germany donated months ago a cargo scanner to be used at a second crossing at Aries in
northern Gaza and urged Israel to allow more aid in.
But Israeli authorities say Aries' crossing will not be open for cargo.
Trucks will be screened there and then escorted south to Karim Shalom, the only operational
crossing into Gaza, for further inspection.
And Asbaba and Pir News, Gaza City.
Anthropics highly anticipated Wall Street debut is set for today.
The company is offering 825 million shares that will begin trading on the NASDAQ.
Anthropics has priced its initial public offering at $83 per share.
The proceeds expected to total $81 billion, putting the company's IPO ahead of SpaceX,
which raised some $75 billion in June.
Choose and Texas singer Ella Langley is this year's big winner at the CMA Awards.
Langley won the top honor entertainer of the year, as well as sweeping the major categories,
including album and song of the year Choose and Texas ranked number one on the Billboard
Hot 100 chart for at least 27 weeks.
I'm Giles Snyder, NPR News.

topics.text: Trump and Xi hold third bilateral meeting in Shenzhen, calling their relationship outstanding
Putin joins Trump and Xi for first-ever trilateral leaders' meeting, agenda includes Ukraine and Iran
House Oversight's Robert Garcia demands Trump aides and family preserve documents ahead of investigations
States of emergency declared in Fort Lauderdale and Broward County after heavy flooding rains
Israel controls Gaza's only operating aid crossing as international pressure grows over winter supplies
Anthropic IPO begins trading on NASDAQ, raising about $81 billion at $83 per share
Ella Langley wins CMA Entertainer of the Year, sweeping major categories with 'Choose and Texas'
